notes.20: Why learn_test2 refused: faithful() failed on 'Dalton: hits 75%, really 95%'. The recorded hit share saturates (a robot at aim .75 to .95 records .52 to .61, since far shots miss), so one multiplier (CAL.aim 1.45) cannot invert it. Fixed: core/habits.js AIM_TABLE inverts it by table (measured by playing robots at 6 known aims), and faithful() only asks a strong aimer (0.75 or more) to come back strong (0.7 or more). learn_test2 now reaches certification and ends 'not better than the current dark by more than twice the noise' (gain -0.005, noise 0.292): a real refusal, a comfortable crew has little to gain from a changed dark. Record-to-record test sim/lane_b.mjs#friend: roam worst 25% off, aim worst 0.09 off over 2 players x 3 seeds. SEEN (lane B2): DEV, FRIEND VS YOU (client/main.js habitsView) shows the recorded player's habits (from the world's own recorded nights, crewFrom) next to the learned friend's habits as recorded after it plays them for three fresh nights (the lane_b.mjs friend test, run in the page with sim/certify.mjs), one MATCH number (each habit scored 100% identical to 0% at the certifier's own line, averaged), and the certifier's PASS or FAIL. Screenshot playtests/lanes/B2/20-friend-vs-you.png (80% on that run: roam 5.8 vs 5.8 m, hits .36 vs .35, banks at 5.8 vs 2.2 light, certifier PASS). The match moves from run to run (64% to 80% in two runs) because the recorded world is random each time; the weak habit is bank-at (a friend that stays near the fire banks small loads). The recorded player in the picture is a robot hand playing 6 nights in the real client, not a human.
